nodes.name: European beech
nodes.desc: The dominant tree of the Perućica primeval forest, where some beeches reach about 60 m. Its nuts are food for many animals, including jays and wild boar.

nodes.name: Silver fir
nodes.desc: A conifer of the coniferous and beech forests on the park's northwestern slopes. Chamois eat conifer needles and bark in winter.

nodes.name: Mountain meadow herbs
nodes.desc: Globeflower and many other flowering herbs of the pastures and meadows above the tree line, part of a flora of about 2,600 plant species.

nodes.name: Dwarf elder
nodes.desc: A tall herb whose berries are eaten by birds, and whose foliage feeds the caterpillars of the Jersey tiger moth.

nodes.name: Balkan chamois
nodes.desc: A goat-antelope of steep rocky ground. It grazes highland grasses and herbs in summer and eats conifer needles and bark in winter.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore for which acorns and beechnuts are key foods in temperate forests. It digs up roots and bulbs and eats carrion.

nodes.name: Eurasian jay
nodes.desc: A woodland crow that eats nuts, seeds and berries as well as small animals.

nodes.name: Common wood pigeon
nodes.desc: A large pigeon that feeds mostly on seeds, buds and berries.

nodes.name: Common chaffinch
nodes.desc: A common forest songbird that eats seeds and berries and feeds insects to its young.

nodes.name: Jersey tiger moth
nodes.desc: A day-flying moth whose caterpillars feed on plants such as dwarf elder.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: An omnivorous crow that scavenges carcasses and is regularly seen in the park.

nodes.name: Common buzzard
nodes.desc: A medium-sized raptor that takes small mammals, birds and reptiles, including snakes.

nodes.name: Red-backed shrike
nodes.desc: A small predatory songbird that hunts insects, lizards and small birds from perches.

nodes.name: Nose-horned viper
nodes.desc: A venomous snake of rocky Balkan slopes that eats lizards, small mammals and birds.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: A largely plant-eating omnivore that also takes wild boar and feeds on carrion, especially in early spring. Bears have been sighted in Perućica.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: A pack hunter whose prey across Eurasia includes red deer, roe deer and wild boar. Wolves have been sighted in Perućica.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: A large raptor reported in Perućica. It eats mostly small mammals, medium-sized birds and reptiles, and also uses carrion.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Summer light drives growth in the forest canopy and on the open pastures above it.

nodes.name: Rain and snowmelt
nodes.desc: Mountain precipitation feeds streams and the glacial lakes of Zelengora, and sustains the forest.

nodes.name: Winter snow
nodes.desc: Deep mountain snow pushes chamois down from the meadows to forested slopes, where they eat conifer needles.

nodes.name: Forest soil
nodes.desc: Leaf litter and dead wood build the soil that the primeval beech and fir forest grows on.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil life
nodes.desc: Fungi and soil organisms break down dead wood, leaves and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil. The park has about 100 edible fungi species.
